title_en: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says
title_zh: 卫生部称，以色列对加沙医院的袭击造成六名巴勒斯坦人死亡
summary: Witnesses say a missile hit a building containing the surgical wards and intensive care units at Nasser hospital, the largest in southern Gaza.
summary_zh: 目击者称，一枚导弹击中了加沙南部最大的纳赛尔医院内设有外科病房和重症监护室的大楼。
body_en: By Rushdi Abualouf , Gaza correspondent , Reporting from Istanbul , David Gritten and Claire Keenan
Six people have been killed and about 30 injured in an Israeli air strike on Nasser hospital in the southern Gaza Strip, the Hamas-run health ministry says.
The hospital's director said two missiles hit a building containing surgical wards and intensive care units overnight, but that one of the missiles did not explode.

The health ministry said medical staff, patients and companions were killed, among them surgeon Dr Rizq Abu Shaira. It condemned the attack as a "flagrant violation of international laws and conventions".
The Israeli military said it targeted a commander of Hamas's armed wing and other fighters who had used the hospital as a "headquarters" to plan attacks on its forces.
Hamas said that Israel was spreading "false narratives" in a "blatant attempt to cover up a new war crime".
Under international law, hospitals have a protected status, but they have been repeatedly targeted during the Gaza war.

Israel accuses Hamas, which retains security control of parts of Gaza not occupied by Israeli troops, of cynically exploiting civilian infrastructure. It says the group stores weapons and runs command and control rooms in hospitals, which Hamas denies.
Israel does not allow international news organisations, including the BBC, into Gaza, making it difficult to verify what is happening in the territory.
The Nasser Medical Complex is located in the city of Khan Younis and is the largest hospital in southern Gaza, serving almost one million people.

In a video posted on social media, a paramedic from the Hamas-run Civil Defence agency who arrived at the building after the strike early on Thursday said a missile penetrated the five-storey structure and hit a room in the surgical department.
Other footage shared by activists showed thick smoke inside the building and extensive destruction on the second floor, where medical equipment and beds had been scattered by an explosion.
The hospital's director, Dr Ahmed al-Fara, later told a news conference that Israeli forces had fired two missiles at the al-Yasin surgery building but that only one exploded.
"What's happened in Nasser Medical Complex is targeting the health sector mainly. We are talking about doctors, we are talking about civilians, we are talking about patients," he said.
"Also, there is... huge damage [to] the infrastructure inside the hospital."
Footage filmed by a freelance journalist working for the BBC showed extensive damage to an operating theatre, wards and a sleeping area for medics, as well as hallways and lifts.
News agencies also published photos that appeared to show an unexploded missile.

Dr Mohammed Qdeih, a general surgery specialist who was wounded in the head, said he and other medical staff had just finished work around 00:30 and had been preparing to go to sleep when there was an explosion.
"My whole body was trapped under the rubble. For a moment, I felt as if I was about to lose consciousness, or that I was about to die," he told the BBC.

"I started struggling to free myself and started calling out, 'Guys! Guys!' I began crawling, trying to pull my leg out from beneath the rubble. I managed to pull myself free. It was dark, there were no lights, nothing at all."
body_zh: 作者：Rushdi Abualouf，加沙记者，伊斯坦布尔报道，David Gritten 和 Claire Keenan
哈马斯卫生部称，以色列对加沙地带南部纳赛尔医院发动空袭，造成 6 人死亡、约 30 人受伤。
该医院院长表示，两枚导弹连夜击中了一座包含外科病房和重症监护室的建筑，但其中一枚导弹没有爆炸。
卫生部表示，医务人员、患者和同伴遇难，其中包括外科医生 Rizq Abu Shaira 博士。它谴责这次袭击“公然违反国际法和公约”。
以色列军方表示，袭击目标是哈马斯武装部队的一名指挥官和其他武装分子，他们利用该医院作为“总部”，计划对其部队发动袭击。
哈马斯表示，以色列正在散布“虚假叙述”，“公然试图掩盖新的战争罪行”。
根据国际法，医院享有受保护地位，但在加沙战争期间却屡次成为攻击目标。
以色列指责哈马斯肆意地利用民用基础设施，哈马斯保留着对未被以色列军队占领的加沙部分地区的安全控制。据称，该组织储存武器并在医院设有指挥和控制室，但哈马斯对此予以否认。
以色列不允许包括 BBC 在内的国际新闻机构进入加沙，因此很难核实该地区正在发生的情况。
纳赛尔医疗中心位于汗尤尼斯市，是加沙南​​部最大的医院，为近百万人提供服务。
在社交媒体上发布的一段视频中，周四早些时候袭击发生后抵达该大楼的哈马斯民防机构的一名护理人员表示，一枚导弹穿透了这座五层楼的建筑，击中了外科部门的一个房间。
活动人士分享的其他视频显示，大楼内浓烟滚滚，二楼遭到严重破坏，医疗设备和床位因爆炸散落一地。
该医院院长艾哈迈德·法拉博士后来在新闻发布会上表示，以色列军队向亚辛手术大楼发射了两枚导弹，但只有一枚爆炸。
“纳赛尔医疗综合体发生的事情主要针对卫生部门。我们正在谈论医生，我们正在谈论平民，我们正在谈论患者，”他说。
“此外，医院内部的基础设施也受到了巨大的破坏。”
BBC 一名自由记者拍摄的视频显示，手术室、病房、医务人员睡眠区以及走廊和电梯均遭到严重损坏。
新闻机构还发布了似乎显示一枚未爆炸导弹的照片。
头部受伤的普外科专家 Mohammed Qdeih 医生表示，他和其他医护人员在 00:30 左右刚刚完成工作，正准备睡觉时发生了爆炸。
“我的整个身体被困在废墟下。有那么一刻，我感觉自己快要失去知觉，或者快要死了，”他告诉 BBC。
“我开始努力挣脱，并开始大喊，‘伙计们！伙计们！’我开始爬行，试图将腿从废墟下拉出来。我设法把自己挣脱出来。天很黑，没有灯光，什么都没有。”

title_en: EU leaders tussle over who to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks
title_zh: 欧盟领导人就派遣谁前往乌克兰和俄罗斯进行和平谈判争论不休
summary: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.
summary_zh: 在刚刚与普京举行会谈的美国特使发表评论后，欧洲现在似乎有可能在谈判桌上占有一席之地。但谁将占据这个席位仍然存在
body_en: European leaders are under pressure to put forward a name to represent them in Ukraine peace talks after US envoy Steve Witkoff told reporters that the Europeans will be present at the next meetings.

When asked by DW during the European Political Community summit in Dublin why Europe should only get one seat at the table while the US gets two, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas responded with a wry, ironic laugh ― clearly a sign of the frustration felt by European leaders about being sidelined thus far.

The summit of 47 European leaders in Dublin comes in the wake of a diplomatic tour by two Donald Trump administration advisers, the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, to talks in Abu Dhabi , followed by a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
The pair then hot-footed their way to Dublin to debrief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelekenskyy .
Zelenskyy and Kushner also said Thursday that Europeans would be at the table for the next talks with Russia on ending the war.

Kallas is one of the figures tipped as most likely to represent the EU in any future talks to end Russia's war against Ukraine , alongside EU Council President Antonio Costa. As yet, the EU hasn’t been able to land on one central figure to send ― many of the national leaders want to be present themselves.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz insisted Europe will be present.
"At the table must be sitting Ukraine, must be sitting the Europeans, must be sitting the Americans, and naturally Russia," he told reporters in Dublin.
But he, like many other leaders, played down the idea of appointing a special envoy for the talks.
Zelenskyy is insistent on European involvement in the peace talks.

"Not directly yet, and not yet when the Russians are at the table," he told the other leaders during the Dublin meetings. "But Europeans are already involved. And we need to make sure that Europe becomes a regular part of these negotiations."

Europe’s division over exactly who should be present has caused a public battle to erupt. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote an excoriating letter to Costa last week, bemoaning the lack of unity.
"By projecting the image of a Europe that is in disarray, we are merely serving the interests of those who want this war to continue," wrote Meloni.
European leaders had even seemed divided over their level of frustration about the situation.

Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Jansa said in Dublin that it was creating a "bad mood" among leaders, however Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs disputed those comments saying, "I don’t feel that."

The palpable fear among the leaders in Dublin is that the US will accept Russia's demands that Europe changes the way it structures its own security, mainly through the NATO military alliance, in exchange for a seat at the table.
Putin said a commitment that Ukraine will never join NATO and even the potential rolling back of the alliance to remove new joiners Finland and Sweden , could be among his demands.

"What do we hear from them [Europeans]?" asked Putin during the meeting with Kushner and Witkoff in Moscow. "That once a peace agreement is signed, they will immediately deploy troops in Ukraine. This is a legitimate target for us, so the war will resume immediately."
This is exactly the kind of rhetoric the European leaders say they are most wary of , especially those in Russia’s direct neighborhood.
body_zh: 在美国特使史蒂夫·威特科夫告诉记者欧洲人将出席下次会议后，欧洲领导人面临压力，要求提出代表他们参加乌克兰和谈的人选。
在都柏林举行的欧洲政治共同体峰会上，当德国之声问及为何欧洲只能在谈判桌上获得一个席位而美国却获得两个席位时，欧盟外交政策负责人卡贾·卡拉斯以苦涩、讽刺的笑声回应——这显然是欧洲领导人对迄今为止被边缘化感到沮丧的迹象。
47位欧洲领导人在都柏林举行峰会之前，唐纳德·特朗普政府的两名顾问、总统的女婿贾里德·库什纳和特使史蒂夫·威特科夫进行了外交访问，前往阿布扎比进行会谈，随后在莫斯科与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京会面。
随后，两人急忙前往都柏林，向乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽莱肯斯基汇报情况。
泽连斯基和库什纳周四还表示，欧洲人将参加与俄罗斯举行的下一次结束战争谈判。
卡拉斯是最有可能与欧盟理事会主席安东尼奥·科斯塔一起代表欧盟参​​加未来结束俄罗斯对乌克兰战争的谈判的人物之一。到目前为止，欧盟还没有找到一位核心人物来派出——许多国家领导人都希望亲自出席。
德国总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨坚称欧洲将出席。
他在都柏林对记者说：“谈判桌上必须有乌克兰，必须有欧洲，必须有美国人，当然还有俄罗斯。”
但与许多其他领导人一样，他淡化了任命特使参加会谈的想法。
泽连斯基坚持要求欧洲参与和平谈判。
他在都柏林会议期间对其他领导人表示：“还没有直接采取行动，而且在俄罗斯坐到谈判桌前也还没有采取行动。” “但欧洲人已经参与其中。我们需要确保欧洲成为这些谈判的常规组成部分。”
欧洲对于到底谁应该出席的分歧导致了一场公开斗争的爆发。意大利总理乔治亚·梅洛尼上周给科斯塔写了一封严厉的信，哀叹缺乏团结。
梅洛尼写道：“通过塑造欧洲混乱的形象，我们只是在为那些希望这场战争继续下去的人的利益服务。”
欧洲领导人甚至似乎因对局势的沮丧程度而存在分歧。
斯洛文尼亚总理雅内兹·扬萨在都柏林表示，这在领导人中制造了“坏情绪”，但拉脱维亚总理安德里斯·库尔伯格对这些言论提出异议，称“我不这么认为”。

都柏林领导人明显担心的是，美国会接受俄罗斯的要求，即欧洲主要通过北约军事联盟改变其自身安全构建方式，以换取在谈判桌上的席位。
普京表示，他的要求可能包括承诺乌克兰永远不会加入北约，甚至可能取消该联盟以消除新加入者芬兰和瑞典。
“我们从他们（欧洲人）那里听到了什么？”普京在莫斯科与库什纳和威特科夫会面时问道。 “一旦签署和平协议，他们将立即在乌克兰部署军队。这对我们来说是合法的目标，因此战争将立即恢复。”
这正是欧洲领导人表示最警惕的言论，尤其是俄罗斯直接邻国的领导人。

title_en: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone in Gulf of Finland
title_zh: 俄罗斯军舰在芬兰湾被乌克兰无人机击中
summary: The attack is thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an open stretch of the Baltic Sea.
summary_zh: 此次袭击被认为是乌克兰无人机首次在波罗的海开阔海域袭击俄罗斯船只。
body_en: Finnish officials have confirmed that a Russian warship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday, although little is known about the strike.
Ukraine's SBU security service said it targeted the ship Naro-Fominsk as part of a broader drone operation against Russia's Ust-Luga oil export depot on the Baltic coast.

The attack, thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an area of the Baltic Sea open to civilian maritime traffic, has raised questions about whether Ukraine could expand its strikes.
Helsinki has been one of Kyiv's closest European allies, and Finnish officials have described the incident as a direct result of Russia's continued full-scale war.
Finland's military has given few details of the incident, but it appears to have taken place in a narrow stretch some distance from the Finnish coast.
The country's Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen was adamant that the situation in the Baltic Sea remained stable and safe and that there was no threat of any kind to marine traffic.
Defence officials are understood to have stressed to Kyiv that the Gulf is a relatively narrow waterway used by oil tankers and civilian vessels, and is also home to subsea data cables.

Ukraine's SBU described the Russian ship as a Buyan-M type small corvette that carried Kalibr and Oniks cruise missiles. There were also unconfirmed reports of Russian combat helicopters being destroyed.

Martin Herem, the defence minister of Estonia, which borders the Gulf, told public broadcaster ERR that the ship was hit at about 05:30 (03:30 GMT) on Wednesday but did not say how it was attacked: "We know that smoke came from the ship afterwards. The ship itself went back towards St Petersburg."
The extent of casualties or damage sustained by the Russian navy ship remains unclear, and Moscow rarely gives such details.

"The Baltic Sea fleet has been untouched up to this point but there seemingly was a window of opportunity for Ukraine and they understandably tried to use it," said military analyst Emil Kastehelmi, co-founder of the Black Bird monitoring group.

Russian and Ukrainian vessels have been repeatedly targeted in the Black Sea since Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022, but even though the latest strike on a ship in the Baltic is unprecedented, Kastehelmi told the BBC he did not consider it a serious escalation.

Ukrainian drones are regularly launched into Russia from northern Ukraine. Several storage tanks at the Ust-Luga terminal are thought to have been hit overnight on Wednesday and fires at the port were visible over the border in Estonia.
Herem said Ukrainian drones attacked the Ust-Luga region from midnight until about 06:00, mostly flying close to the Estonian border but still in Russian airspace.
He added that one drone had entered Estonian airspace briefly from Latvia and then headed towards Russia.
Nato aircraft based in the Baltic states were in the air at the time, but Herem said it had not been considered safe for them to destroy the drones.

Ukrainian foreign ministry spokesman Heorhiy Tykhyy said late on Wednesday that Moscow's allegations that Kyiv had used the airspace of the Baltic states to attack Russia were "baseless", although he acknowledged "incidents might occur when Russia diverts drones from its airspace using electronic warfare".
body_zh: 芬兰官员证实，一艘俄罗斯军舰周三在芬兰湾遭到袭击，但对这次袭击知之甚少。
乌克兰SBU安全部门表示，它以Naro-Fominsk号为目标，这是针对俄罗斯波罗的海沿岸的Ust-Luga石油出口库的更广泛无人机行动的一部分。
这次袭击被认为是乌克兰无人机首次在波罗的海对民用海上交通开放的地区袭击俄罗斯船只，引发了人们对乌克兰是否可以扩大袭击范围的疑问。
赫尔辛基一直是基辅最亲密的欧洲盟友之一，芬兰官员称这一事件是俄罗斯持续全面战争的直接结果。
芬兰军方没有透露这起事件的细节，但事件似乎发生在距芬兰海岸一段距离的狭窄地带。
该国外交部长埃琳娜·瓦尔托宁坚称波罗的海局势保持稳定和安全，海上交通不存在任何形式的威胁。
据了解，国防官员向基辅强调，海湾是一条相对狭窄的水道，供油轮和民用船只使用，也是海底数据电缆的所在地。
乌克兰SBU将这艘俄罗斯舰艇描述为Buyan-M型小型护卫舰，携带“口径”和“奥尼克斯”巡航导弹。还有未经证实的报道称俄罗斯战斗直升机被摧毁。
与海湾接壤的爱沙尼亚国防部长马丁·赫勒姆 (Martin Herem) 向公共广播公司 ERR 表示，该船于周三 05:30（格林威治标准时间 03:30）左右遭到袭击，但没有透露是如何受到袭击的：“我们知道随后船冒出烟雾。船本身返回了圣彼得堡。”
俄罗斯海军舰艇造成的伤亡或损坏程度尚不清楚，莫斯科也很少提供此类细节。
黑鸟监测组织联合创始人、军事分析家埃米尔·卡斯泰赫米表示：“到目前为止，波罗的海舰队尚未受到影响，但乌克兰似乎有一个机会之窗，他们试图利用它，这是可以理解的。”
自2022年2月俄罗斯开始全面入侵以来，俄罗斯和乌克兰船只在黑海多次成为攻击目标，但尽管最近波罗的海一艘船只遭受的袭击是史无前例的，但卡斯泰赫米告诉BBC，他并不认为这是一次严重的升级。
乌克兰无人机定期从乌克兰北部发射到俄罗斯。据信乌斯季卢加码头的几个储罐周三夜间遭到袭击，爱沙尼亚边境上空可以看到港口起火。
赫雷姆说，乌克兰无人机从午夜到06:00左右袭击了乌斯季卢加地区，大部分飞行靠近爱沙尼亚边境，但仍在俄罗斯领空。
他补充说，一架无人机从拉脱维亚短暂进入爱沙尼亚领空，然后飞往俄罗斯。
当时，驻扎在波罗的海国家的北约飞机正在空中飞行，但赫勒姆表示，他们认为摧毁这些无人机并不安全。
乌克兰外交部发言人赫奥希·蒂赫伊周三晚间表示，莫斯科关于基辅利用波罗的海国家领空攻击俄罗斯的指控“毫无根据”，尽管他承认“当俄罗斯使用电子战将无人机从其领空转移时可能会发生事件”。

title_en: Israel strikes Gaza hospital, says Hamas senior figure inside
title_zh: 哈马斯内部高级人士称，以色列袭击了加沙医院
summary: Israel says Hamas was using the hospital as a military command center, while Palestinian officials report at least six people killed, including a surgeon. The strike comes amid an increasingly fragile ceasefire.
summary_zh: 以色列称哈马斯将该医院用作军事指挥中心，而巴勒斯坦官员报告称至少有六人死亡，其中包括一名增援人员
body_en: Israel hits Gaza hospital, says Hamas senior figure inside
Israel said it had targeted a senior Hamas member in a Gaza hospital in an overnight airstrike which reportedly killed six people.
According to the Israeli military, Muhammad Abu Ismail and other militants from the Islamist group had been operating a command center inside the Nasser hospital in Khan Yunis.
Gaza's civil defense service said at least six people were killed, including a surgeon and more than 20 were wounded. It said that parts of several floors were severely damaged or destroyed.
During war, hospitals are protected under international humanitarian law, although they can lose that protection if they are used for military purposes.
Israel says hospital used for terrorist activities

In a statement on Thursday, the Israeli military (IDF) said, without providing evidence, that Hamas was "operating within Nasser Hospital in Khan Yunis" and were using the complex "as a hub for military and terrorist activities against IDF troops and Israel."

The IDF identified the targeted senior Hamas member as Abu Ismail, adding he "was responsible for directing terrorist attacks against Israeli civilians & IDF troops and for holding numerous hostages captive throughout the war."
The IDF said the hospital was used for storing weapons, to conduct interrogation, operate command-and-control rooms as well as to shelter terrorists.
The Gaza Health Ministry said the Israeli airstrike hit the surgery department, killing six people including surgeon Rizk Abu Sharia.
News agency Reuters reported seeing footage from inside the hospital showing extensive damage with debris scattered around rooms and equipment.
Wounded people were also seen in the wreckage while several bodies were being carried away as firefighters worked to clear the scene.
Hamas has described the strike as a "fully-fledged war crime."
Since the beginning of the war in 2023, Israeli forces have attacked several hospitals in the Gaza Strip.
The war on Hamas in Gaza began in October 2023 after Hamas-led militants attacked southern Israel , killing around 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages.
Since then, more than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the Gaza Health Ministry, whose figures are generally considered reliable by the international community.
More than 1.6 million residents of Gaza's 2.1-million population now live in tents or other makeshift shelters due to Israel's war in the enclave.

A ceasefire came into effect in October 2025, but attacks have continued since then. While Israel says Hamas is trying to regroup, the Palestinian militant group says it's committed to the ceasefire and that Israel is trying to undermine the agreement.
Hamas is recognized as a terrorist organization by the EU, the US and several Arab states.
Gaza: Rains add misery to humanitarian catastrophe
body_zh: 哈马斯内部高级人士称，以色列袭击了加沙医院
以色列表示，它在夜间空袭中瞄准了加沙一家医院的一名哈马斯高级成员，据报道造成六人死亡。
据以色列军方称，穆罕默德·阿布·伊斯梅尔和该伊斯兰组织的其他武装分子一直在汗尤尼斯的纳赛尔医院内运营一个指挥中心。
加沙民防部门表示，至少有六人死亡，其中包括一名外科医生，另有二十多人受伤。据称，有几层楼的部分区域遭到严重损坏或毁坏。
在战争期间，医院受到国际人道法的保护，尽管如果它们被用于军事目的，它们可能会失去这种保护。
以色列称医院被用于恐怖活动
以色列军方在周四的一份声明中表示，在没有提供证据的情况下，哈马斯“在汗尤尼斯的纳赛尔医院内开展活动”，并利用该建筑群“作为针对以色列国防军和以色列的军事和恐怖活动的中心”。
以色列国防军确认目标哈马斯高级成员为阿布·伊斯梅尔，并补充说他“负责指挥针对以色列平民和以色列国防军部队的恐怖袭击，并在整个战争期间扣押了大量人质”。
以色列国防军表示，该医院用于储存武器、进行审讯、操作指挥控制室以及庇护恐怖分子。
加沙卫生部表示，以色列空袭袭击了外科部门，造成包括外科医生里兹克·阿布·沙里亚在内的六人死亡。
路透社报道称，从医院内部拍摄的视频显示，房间和设备周围散落着碎片，造成严重损坏。
残骸中还看到了伤者，消防队员正在清理现场，同时还有几具尸体被运走。
哈马斯将这次袭击描述为“彻底的战争罪行”。
自2023年战争爆发以来，以色列军队袭击了加沙地带的多家医院。
2023 年 10 月，哈马斯领导的武装分子袭击了以色列南部，造成约 1,200 人死亡，并劫持了 251 名人质，加沙地带的哈马斯战争由此开始。
据加沙卫生部称，自那时以来，加沙已有超过74,000人被杀，国际社会普遍认为该数字是可靠的。
由于以色列在加沙飞地发动战争，目前加沙 210 万人口中有超过 160 万居民住在帐篷或其他临时避难所中。
停火于 2025 年 10 月生效，但此后袭击事件仍在继续。虽然以色列称哈马斯正试图重组，但巴勒斯坦激进组织却表示其致力于停火，而以色列正试图破坏该协议。
哈马斯被欧盟、美国和几个阿拉伯国家认定为恐怖组织。

title_en: Scandal-hit Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits, plunging AI chipmaking giant into turmoil
title_zh: 丑闻缠身的英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋辞职，AI芯片制造巨头陷入混乱
summary: US lawmakers now want to question Huang over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy.
summary_zh: 美国立法者现在想质问黄是否与一名中国间谍有所谓的关系。
body_en: By Kali Hays , Technology reporter and Lily Jamali , North America Technology correspondent
Jensen Huang has abruptly quit as chief executive of AI chipmaking giant Nvidia after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, sending shockwaves from Silicon Valley to Capitol Hill.
Nvidia is now under scrutiny from US lawmakers in Washington DC demanding Huang answer questions over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy.
One of the world's most valuable companies as a result of the AI boom, Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines.
Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress, called an emergency meeting of her executive team to discuss the company's future.
His alleged conduct not only potentially crossed professional boundaries, but has made Nvidia the target of questions from US politicians who have expressed concern about national security risks.

Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation).
On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive.

Alice Huang worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected those allegations as a smear.
And US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing.
Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons, along with other Democrats on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, publicly demanded that Huang brief Congress on his alleged affair.
If he refuses to appear voluntarily before any committee that calls him, he could be subpoenaed, one Senate staff member told the BBC.
Representatives of Nvidia have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday.
According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company.
Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close.

Huang had been widely expected to weather the scandal after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company.
It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said.
Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public.
Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared.
body_zh: 作者：Kali Hays，科技记者和 Lily Jamali，北美科技记者
在涉嫌婚外情被曝光后，黄仁勋突然辞去了人工智能芯片制造巨头英伟达首席执行官的职务，震惊了整个硅谷和国会山。
英伟达目前正在华盛顿接受美国立法者的审查，要求黄回答有关他涉嫌的关系是否与中国间谍有关系的问题。
因人工智能热潮而成为全球最有价值公司之一的英伟达，在丑闻占据头条新闻的短短五天内，其股票市值就损失了 5500 亿美元（4150 亿英镑）。
英伟达临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)召开了执行团队紧急会议，讨论公司的未来。
他被指控的行为不仅可能跨越了专业界限，而且使英伟达成为美国政界人士质疑的目标，这些政界人士对国家安全风险表示担忧。
黄自 1993 年以来一直是 Nvidia 的公众形象，周日，在有报道称他与疑似中国间谍的爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang)（无亲属关系）发生婚外情后，他于周日承认对妻子“不忠”。
周三，据报道他又有了第二段恋情，这次是与英伟达的一名高管。
Alice Huang 曾担任新加坡公司 Megaspeed 的高管。据《纽约时报》报道，她被怀疑是中国的情报人员。中国否认这些指控，称其为诽谤。
美国司法部长托德·布兰奇周四表示，司法部尚未就爱丽丝·黄参与北京间谍活动得出任何结论。
参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦（Elizabeth Warren）和克里斯·库恩斯（Chris Coons）以及众议院外交事务委员会的其他民主党人公开要求黄向国会通报他所指控的事件。
一名参议院工作人员告诉英国广播公司，如果他拒绝自愿出席任何召唤他的委员会，他可能会被传唤。
自周三以来，英伟达代表多次拒绝置评。黄的个人代表周四也拒绝置评。
据美国媒体报道，黄的第二次恋情是与长期担任英伟达高管的金伯利·鲍威尔(Kimberly Powell)发生的，后者在公司内部直接向他汇报。
消息人士告诉 BBC，英伟达员工注意到两人关系异常亲密。
在第一起丑闻曝光后，人们普遍预计黄将安然度过这起丑闻，尽管英伟达宣布已对其首席执行官是否是“外国情报工作的目标”展开调查。
英伟达的一名现任员工告诉 BBC，公司内部的普通员工或多或少对有关他不忠的最初报道不予理睬。
该人士表示，直到黄与英伟达高管的恋情被公开后，员工们才开始觉得“这太疯狂了”。
另一名英伟达员工表示，他们被告知不要与媒体交谈或以其他方式公开评论此事。
随着英伟达股价飙升，许多员工通过兑现其股票而获得了数百万美元的薪酬。

title_en: An Israeli strike on a Gaza hospital kills 6 people, including a doctor and a child
title_zh: 以色列对加沙一家医院的袭击造成 6 人死亡，其中包括一名医生和一名儿童
summary: The victims included a surgeon, and dozens more were injured. Israel said it was targeting a Hamas commander and other militants. The commander was not found among the dead.
summary_zh: 受害者包括一名外科医生，还有数十人受伤。以色列表示，其目标是一名哈马斯指挥官和其他武装分子。指挥官没有
body_en: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills 6, including doctor and child : NPR

Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills 6, including doctor and child The victims included a surgeon, and dozens more were injured. Israel said it was targeting a Hamas commander and other militants. The commander was not found among the dead.
Medical staff inspect damage to Nasser Hospital after it was hit by an Israeli airstrike overnight in Khan Younis, Gaza Strip on Thursday. Abdel Kareem Hana/AP hide caption

KHAN YOUNIS, Gaza Strip — An Israeli airstrike hit one of the main hospitals still operating in the Gaza Strip on Thursday, killing six people, including a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy, Gaza's Health Ministry said.
Gaza struck by deadly storm; Israel debates rare coalition with Palestinian citizens
The Israeli military said the strike on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza was targeting a Hamas commander and other militants. The commander it identified was not among the dead.

The strike hit the hospital's surgical wing, the ministry and witnesses said. Footage showed several wards and operating rooms heavily damaged or destroyed, with debris scattered across hospital beds and equipment and rebar dangling from holes in the ceiling. At least 28 people were wounded.
Among the dead were Dr. Rizk Abu Shaira, a general surgeon, and at least two patients, one of them the 13-year-old, according to the ministry.
Mourners attend the funeral of Khalid Abu Anza, 53, who was killed in an overnight Israeli airstrike on Nasser Hospital, in Khan Younis, Gaza Strip, Thursday. Abdel Kareem Hana/AP hide caption

Gaza's healthcare infrastructure has been decimated by a yearslong war whose trajectory is not expected to be altered by the outcome of Israel's recent election. The Israeli military has raided or laid siege to hospitals across the territory, accusing Hamas of using them as command centers and to hide fighters. Israel has also destroyed medical equipment and supplies and killed or detained hundreds of healthcare workers.
Two beaches, just miles apart, show how different daily life is in Israel and Gaza
In armed conflict, hospitals and their staff are protected under international humanitarian law. A hospital can lose its protected status, however, if it is used for military purposes.
Work is halted in several areas of the hospital after the strike
British surgeon Goher Rahbour, who is volunteering at Nasser Hospital, said that the strike occurred just after midnight and shook the whole building.
"It was extremely smoky," said Rahbour, who was on the fourth floor of the surgical department at the time. The recovery area on the same floor was reduced to rubble, he said.
He said he had been operating alongside Abu Shaira just hours before the strike. "Lovely guy, happy and smiling," Rahbour said.
People look at remnants of an Israeli projectile after an overnight airstrike hit Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, Gaza Strip, Thursday. Abdel Kareem Hana/AP hide caption

Ahmed al-Farra, a doctor and the general director of the hospital, said no warning came before the attack, but the Israeli army said it had warned "on several occasions, including recently, that the military activity at the hospital be halted."

Al-Farra said surgeries and other services had been suspended because of damage to the building where medical personnel were already struggling to provide care due to supply shortages and "miserable" conditions.
body_zh: 以色列对加沙医院的袭击造成 6 人死亡，其中包括医生和儿童：NPR
以色列对加沙医院的袭击造成包括医生和儿童在内的 6 人死亡，受害者包括一名外科医生，另有数十人受伤。以色列表示，其目标是一名哈马斯指挥官和其他武装分子。死者中没有发现指挥官。
星期四，加沙地带汗尤尼斯的纳赛尔医院遭到以色列连夜空袭，医务人员正在检查其受损情况。阿卜杜勒·卡里姆·哈纳/美联社隐藏标题栏
加沙地带汗尤尼斯——加沙卫生部称，周四，以色列空袭袭击了加沙地带仍在运营的一家主要医院，造成六人死亡，其中包括一名外科医生和一名 13 岁男孩。
加沙遭受致命风暴袭击；以色列与巴勒斯坦公民讨论罕见的联盟
以色列军方表示，对加沙南部纳赛尔医院的袭击目标是一名哈马斯指挥官和其他武装分子。其确认的指挥官并不在死者之中。
卫生部和目击者称，这次袭击袭击了医院的外科部门。视频显示，几间病房和手术室严重受损或被毁，医院病床和设备上散落着碎片，天花板上的洞里悬挂着钢筋。至少28人受伤。
据卫生部称，死者包括普通外科医生 Rizk Abu Shaira 医生和至少两名患者，其中一名 13 岁。
周四，哀悼者参加 53 岁哈立德·阿布·安扎 (Khalid Abu Anza) 的葬礼，他在以色列连夜空袭加沙地带汗尤尼斯的纳赛尔医院时丧生。阿卜杜勒·卡里姆·哈纳/美联社隐藏标题栏
加沙的医疗基础设施已被长达数年的战争摧毁，预计以色列最近的选举结果不会改变其轨迹。以色列军方袭击或围攻了该地区各地的医院，指责哈马斯将它们用作指挥中心并隐藏武装分子。以色列还摧毁了医疗设备和用品，并杀害或拘留了数百名医护人员。
相距仅几英里的两个海滩展示了以色列和加沙的日常生活有多么不同
在武装冲突中，医院及其工作人员受到国际人道法的保护。然而，如果医院用于军事目的，则可能会失去其受保护地位。
罢工后，医院的多个区域停止工作
在纳赛尔医院做志愿者的英国外科医生戈赫·拉布尔（Goher Rahbour）表示，罢工发生在午夜过后，整座大楼都震动了。
“烟雾非常大，”当时在外科四楼的拉布尔说。他说，同一层的恢复区已变成废墟。
他说，就在袭击发生前几个小时，他一直在与阿布·沙伊拉一起行动。 “可爱的家伙，快乐，微笑，”拉布尔说。
周四，加沙地带汗尤尼斯的纳赛尔医院遭到连夜空袭，人们在观看以色列炮弹的残余物。阿卜杜勒·卡里姆·哈纳/美联社隐藏标题栏
该医院院长、医生艾哈迈德·法拉表示，袭击发生前没有发出任何警告，但以色列军方表示，已“多次警告，包括最近，停止在医院的军事活动”。
法拉表示，由于建筑物受损，手术和其他服务已暂停，由于供应短缺和“悲惨”的条件，医务人员已经在努力提供护理。

title_en: China rules out hosting Cop33 climate summit in 2028
title_zh: 中国排除在2028年举办Cop33气候峰会的可能性
summary: Decision disappoints experts hoping for world’s biggest emitter to take global lead on climate crisis China has ruled out hosting the Cop33 UN climate summit in 2028 after months of deliberations, leaving the field open for other Asian countries to hold it, th
summary_zh: 这一决定令专家们失望，他们希望世界最大的排放国在气候危机上发挥全球领导作用，中国已排除主办第33届联合国气候变化大会
body_en: Decision disappoints experts hoping for world’s biggest emitter to take global lead on climate crisis
China has ruled out hosting the Cop33 UN climate summit in 2028 after months of deliberations, leaving the field open for other Asian countries to hold it, the Guardian understands.

The decision will disappoint many countries and climate experts, who had hoped the world’s biggest emitter would take the lead on the global stage, as the US under Donald Trump has vacated all forms of international cooperation on the climate .

Al Gore, the former US vice-president, was among those left disheartened by the decision. “I would be very much in favour of that idea [of China hosting the summit],” he told the Guardian. “It’s too bad.”

China is in the midst of an economic transformation , from being heavily dependent on coal to becoming an “electro state”. John Kerry, the former US secretary of state, told the Guardian that China was leaving the rest of the world behind in forging and using the low-carbon technologies of the future.
Renewable energy generation capacity has now outstripped coal in China, and its greenhouse gas emissions appear to have declined slightly this year.

Sales of electric vehicles in the country have also taken off, making up nearly two-thirds of the market last month, and China’s clean energy industries drove more than 90% of the country’s investment growth last year .
The rules of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) mean an Asian country should host in 2028.

Gareth Redmond-King, the international lead at the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit thinktank, said China’s position as an industrial powerhouse would have made it a formidable contender to hold the summit.
“It would undoubtedly be significant for the world’s biggest emitter and second-biggest economy to host a climate Cop,” he said.

“They’re leading the world on investment, manufacture and deployment of clean energy tech, and their emissions have started to tick down. As a leadership story, China hosting Cop33 would be a big deal.”

It is not clear why China has decided against hosting the conference, but several experts that spoke to the Guardian suggested that the US electoral cycle was likely to have been a factor. The next US presidential election will take place on 7 November 2028, and Cop33 is scheduled for 6 to 17 November that year.

After the strong showing by Democrats in the recent midterm elections, in which voter concern over the climate crisis was thought to be a factor , the Democrats will be hoping to elect a climate-friendly president in 2028. But even if they succeed, Trump will still be in office until the following January.
The US president rejects climate science and withdrew the US from the Paris agreement, and is also withdrawing from its parent treaty, the 1992 UNFCCC.

China seeks to be seen as a leader among developing countries, but has been wary of stepping into the gap left by the US. Under the Democratic presidents Joe Biden and Barack Obama, the US and China enjoyed a close partnership on climate issues , setting joint targets on reducing methane and developing clean technology.
UK ministers have no plans to publish explosive report on climate crisis

Cop33 will be an important meeting because it will include the “global stocktake” – a mechanism under the 2015 Paris climate agreement that examines countries’ progress on cutting emissions in line with the goal of limiting global temperature rises to 1.5C.
That limit is now certain to be surpassed, but experts say countries should now try to minimise the temperature “ overshoot ”, to avoid worse ravages from extreme weather.

India’s government considered offering to host Cop33 for several months earlier this year, but also decided against it. India’s coal use has been increasing, even as the country exceeds its own renewable energy targets.
body_zh: 这一决定令专家们失望，他们希望世界上最大的排放国在气候危机方面发挥全球领导作用
据《卫报》了解，经过数月的考虑，中国已排除在 2028 年举办第 33 届联合国气候变化峰会的可能性，为其他亚洲国家举办该峰会留下了空间。
这一决定将使许多国家和气候专家感到失望，他们原本希望世界上最大的排放国能够在全球舞台上发挥带头作用，因为唐纳德·特朗普领导下的美国已经放弃了一切形式的气候国际合作。
美国前副总统阿尔·戈尔 (Al Gore) 也是对这一决定感到沮丧的人之一。 “我非常赞成[中国主办峰会]的想法，”他告诉卫报。 “太糟糕了。”
中国正处于经济转型之中，从严重依赖煤炭到成为“电力国家”。美国前国务卿约翰·克里 (John Kerry) 向《卫报》表示，中国在打造和使用未来低碳技术方面正在将世界其他国家抛在后面。
中国的可再生能源发电能力现已超过煤炭，其温室气体排放量今年似乎略有下降。
中国电动汽车的销量也开始腾飞，上个月占据了近三分之二的市场份额，中国清洁能源产业带动了去年全国投资增长的90%以上。
《联合国气候变化框架公约》(UNFCCC) 的规则规定，2028 年主办权应由亚洲国家主办。
能源与气候情报机构智囊团国际负责人加雷思·雷蒙德-金表示，中国作为工业强国的地位将使其成为举办此次峰会的有力竞争者。
他说：“对于世界上最大的排放国和第二大经济体来说，接待一位气候警察无疑意义重大。”
“他们在清洁能源技术的投资、制造和部署方面处于世界领先地位，而且他们的排放量已经开始下降。作为一个领导故事，中国主办第三十三届缔约方会议将是一件大事。”
目前尚不清楚中国决定不主办这次会议的原因，但接受《卫报》采访的几位专家表示，美国选举周期可能是一个因素。下届美国总统选举将于 2028 年 11 月 7 日举行，第 33 次缔约方会议定于当年 11 月 6 日至 17 日举行。
民主党在最近的中期选举中表现强劲，选民对气候危机的担忧被认为是一个因素，民主党希望在2028年选出一位气候友好型总统。但即使他们成功，特朗普仍将在任到明年一月。
美国总统拒绝接受气候科学，让美国退出《巴黎协定》，同时也退出了其母条约——1992 年《联合国气候变化框架公约》。
中国寻求被视为发展中国家的领导者，但一直对填补美国留下的空白持谨慎态度。在民主党总统乔·拜登和巴拉克·奥巴马的领导下，美国和中国在气候问题上建立了密切的伙伴关系，制定了减少甲烷排放和开发清洁技术的共同目标。
英国部长们没有计划发布有关气候危机的爆炸性报告
第三十三届缔约方会议将是一次重要的会议，因为它将包括“全球盘点”——2015 年巴黎气候协议下的一项机制，旨在审查各国在将全球气温上升限制在 1.5 摄氏度的目标上减排的进展情况。
现在肯定会超过这一限制，但专家表示，各国现在应该努力尽量减少气温“超调”，以避免极端天气造成更严重的破坏。
印度政府曾考虑在今年早些时候主办第三十三届缔约方会议几个月，但最终决定反对。印度的煤炭使用量一直在增加，尽管该国已经超出了自己的可再生能源目标。

title_en: Palestinian baby dies from cold in Gaza amid Israeli restrictions on aid
title_zh: 以色列限制援助，巴勒斯坦婴儿在加沙冻死
summary: The baby's father said he died of hypothermia overnight in their family's tent in southern Gaza.
summary_zh: 婴儿的父亲说，他在加沙南部自家的帐篷里因体温过低而死亡。
body_en: Palestinian baby dies from cold in Gaza amid Israeli restrictions on aid | Climate News | Al Jazeera
Share Palestinian baby dies from cold in Gaza amid Israeli restrictions on aid on social media

A Palestinian infant has died from the cold in a tent sheltering his displaced family in southern Gaza, his father and a doctor said, as Israel continues to impose severe restrictions on winter supplies to the war-ravaged territory.
Nine-month-old Kinan Ahmed Raqiq “died from hypothermia” in Khan Younis, in the southern region of the enclave, a doctor who spoke on he condition of anonymity told the AFP news agency on Thursday.

Ahmed Raqiq, the baby’s father, told AFP that Kinan died after cold temperatures hit Gaza overnight.
“I woke up only to see his skin had turned blue so I rushed him to Nasser Hospital, but he had already died from hypothermia and frozen to death,” he said.
“I am in complete shock. I found myself holding my son wrapped in a burial shroud,” he said outside the hospital, dried tears on his face as he held his son wrapped in a white sheet.
Gaza’s Civil Defence spokesman, Mahmoud Basal, confirmed the infant’s death after exposure to extreme cold, Palestinian news network Al-Quds reported.

The death comes as the United Kingdom, Qatar and Jordan led a coalition of more than 50 countries and organisations calling on Israel to provide immediate entry of critical items for shelter, fuel, water, sanitation and health to Gaza.

With winter arriving, the group said, “far too many people in Gaza are still without adequate shelter, and risk exposure to hypothermia, respiratory infections, waterborne diseases and other preventable illnesses”.
The statement echoed recent criticism of Israel over its restrictions by the United States-led Board of Peace and United Nations humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher.

Responding to the Board of Peace, Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that Israel had allowed in supplies including 91,000 tents and that “Hamas alone is responsible for the suffering of the people of Gaza.”

As well as the cold, Gaza has experienced flooding this week following heavy rains, affecting tens of thousands of people’s tents. Five people, including three children, died the day after the flooding when a sandy embankment eroded and collapsed onto their tents.
The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said that as of November 8, 26,000 households were affected by storms.
Around 65 percent of Gaza’s people are still living displaced in tents or other temporary shelter, OCHA said.
James Elder, spokesman on Gaza for the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF), warned that the flooding was just the beginning of the cold season.
“It’s very important to know how bad things are in Gaza. It’s not yet winter,” Elder said.
body_zh: 以色列限制援助，巴勒斯坦婴儿在加沙冻死气候新闻|半岛电视台
由于以色列限制社交媒体上的援助，巴勒斯坦婴儿在加沙冻死
一名巴勒斯坦婴儿的父亲和一名医生表示，一名巴勒斯坦婴儿在加沙南部为流离失所的家人提供庇护的帐篷内因寒冷死亡，以色列继续严格限制向饱受战争蹂躏的领土提供冬季物资。
周四，一位不愿透露姓名的医生告诉法新社，九个月大的基南·艾哈迈德·拉奇克在飞地南部地区的汗尤尼斯“死于体温过低”。
共 3 项 第 1 项（共 3 项） 加沙如何应对又一个严冬？
列表 2（共 3 个）“我们的邻居消失了”：加沙幸存者讲述致命洪水的恐怖
list 3 of 3 加沙基础设施倒塌使居民在洪水面前毫无防御能力
婴儿的父亲艾哈迈德·拉奇克告诉法新社，基南在寒冷的气温一夜之间袭击加沙后死亡。
“我醒来时发现他的皮肤已经变成蓝色，所以我赶紧把他送往纳赛尔医院，但他已经因体温过低而被冻死，”他说。
“我完全震惊了。我发现自己抱着裹着裹尸布的儿子，”他在医院外说道，他抱着裹着白床单的儿子，脸上的泪水已干。
据巴勒斯坦新闻网 Al-Quds 报道，加沙民防发言人马哈茂德·巴萨尔 (Mahmoud Basal) 证实婴儿因暴露在极寒环境中而死亡。
死亡事件发生之际，英国、卡塔尔和约旦领导了一个由50多个国家和组织组成的联盟，呼吁以色列立即向加沙提供住房、燃料、水、卫生和健康等关键物品。
该组织表示，随着冬季的到来，“加沙仍有太多人没有足够的住所，并面临着体温过低、呼吸道感染、水传播疾病和其他可预防疾病的风险”。
该声明呼应了美国领导的和平委员会和联合国人道主义事务负责人汤姆·弗莱彻最近对以色列限制措施的批评。
以色列看守总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡在回应和平委员会时表示，以色列已允许包括 91,000 个帐篷在内的物资进入，“加沙人民的苦难仅由哈马斯负责。”
除了寒冷之外，加沙本周还遭遇暴雨后的洪水，影响了数万人的帐篷。洪水发生后的第二天，沙质堤坝被侵蚀并倒塌压垮了他们的帐篷，导致五人死亡，其中包括三名儿童。
联合国人道主义事务协调办公室（OCHA）表示，截至11月8日，已有2.6万户家庭受到风暴影响。
人道协调厅表示，约 65% 的加沙民众仍然流离失所，住在帐篷或其他临时住所中。
联合国儿童基金会（UNICEF）加沙发言人詹姆斯·埃尔德警告说，洪水只是寒冷季节的开始。
“了解加沙的情况有多糟糕非常重要。现在还不是冬天，”埃尔德说。

title_en: Hegseth awards medal to war memorial guard who reprimanded him and group
title_zh: 赫格斯向斥责他和团体的战争纪念卫兵颁发奖章
summary: Specialist Thomas Iglesias had shouted at Hegseth's group to be quiet after they could be heard talking and laughing at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.
summary_zh: 在听到赫格斯一行人在无名烈士墓前有说有笑后，专家托马斯·伊格莱西亚斯向他们大声喊叫，要求他们保持安静。
body_en: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has awarded a medal to the guard who reprimanded his group at Arlington National Cemetery.

A video of a Veterans Day observance event on Wednesday showed Hegseth, his wife, and senior advisers laughing and talking while posing for photos in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier before the guard told them to be quiet.
In a statement, the Pentagon later announced that Hegseth had given Specialist Thomas Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal "for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier".
Photos shared on the defence secretary's X account showed him presenting the medal to Iglesias.

He was accompanied by others whom the Pentagon identified as members of the 3rd US Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, which is responsible for holding vigil over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.
"We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist. Carry on Patriots," the accompanying text on Hegseth's post reads.

In the video, the army sentinel on duty later identified as Iglesias can be seen stepping towards Hegseth's group and shouting: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times."
Image source, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth/X
The Arlington National Cemetery etiquette requests that visitors speak quietly and do not engage in disrespectful or disorderly conduct.
The tomb, which is one of the country's most sacred war memorials, marks the final resting place of an unknown soldier who was killed in World War I.
Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell later said in a statement: "While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum."
"The Secretary and the entire Department have always honoured - and will always honour - the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe."
A service member from the 3rd Infantry Regiment stands watch over the tomb 24 hours a day and has done so since 1948.
It is not unusual for them to admonish visitors to the site, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News. They reportedly do so a few times a day.
Earlier, President Donald Trump, Vice-President JD Vance and other top officials attended the annual wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery.

During his speech at the ceremony, Trump offered his gratitude to uniformed service members who have fought for the country. He also touted what he sees as his administration's success in the Iran war.
"Under this administration, and it was about time, somebody fought back. All of us fought back," he said.
"And we won," Trump said of the Iran war. "It's just a question of when we want to end it. We want to make sure we have a total victory, not a 93% victory."
Trump also pointed out Hegseth during the ceremony, saying he's done a "fantastic job" as defence secretary.

Trump has repeatedly defended Hegseth amid Democratic lawmakers' push to impeach him. On Tuesday, an effort to impeach the defence secretary under accusations that he waged war on Iran without congressional authorisation failed on Capitol Hill .
body_zh: 美国国防部长皮特·赫格斯向在阿灵顿国家公墓斥责其团队的警卫颁发了一枚奖章。
周三退伍军人节纪念活动的视频显示，赫格斯、他的妻子和高级顾问在无名烈士墓前有说有笑地摆姿势拍照，随后警卫让他们保持安静。
五角大楼后来在一份声明中宣布，赫格塞斯授予专家托马斯·伊格莱西亚斯联合服役嘉奖奖章，以表彰他“在无名烈士墓中履行的职责”。
国防部长 X 账户上分享的照片显示，他向伊格莱西亚斯颁发了奖章。
陪同他的还有其他人，五角大楼确认他们是美国第三步兵团的成员，该团被称为“老卫士”，负责为无名烈士墓守夜。
“我们热爱士兵。我们热爱标准。干得好，专家。继续爱国者，”赫格斯帖子上的附文写道。
在视频中，可以看到后来被确认为伊格莱西亚斯的军队哨兵走向赫格斯的队伍，并喊道：“所有访客将始终保持沉默和尊重的气氛。”
图片来源，战争部长 Pete Hegseth/X
阿灵顿国家公墓礼仪要求游客安静说话，不要做出不尊重或扰乱秩序的行为。
这座坟墓是该国最神圣的战争纪念碑之一，标志着一位在第一次世界大战中阵亡的无名士兵的最后安息之地。
五角大楼首席发言人肖恩·帕内尔后来在一份声明中表示：“在纪念这个庄严的日子时，一名士兵正确而恭敬地提醒大家保持礼仪。”
“国务卿和整个部门一直尊重并将永远尊重我们的军人为保护美国安全而做出的牺牲。”
自 1948 年以来，第 3 步兵团的一名军人每天 24 小时守卫这座坟墓。
据英国广播公司美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司新闻报道，他们警告该网站的访问者并不罕见。据报道，他们每天都会这样做几次。
此前，美国总统特朗普、副总统万斯等高级官员出席了在公墓举行的一年一度的敬献花圈仪式。
在仪式上的讲话中，特朗普向为国家而战的军人表示感谢。他还称赞他的政府在伊朗战争中取得了成功。
“在本届政府的领导下，是时候有人反击了。我们所有人都反击了，”他说。
“我们赢了，”特朗普谈到伊朗战争时说道。 “这只是我们什么时候结束的问题。我们要确保我们取得全面胜利，而不是93%的胜利。”
特朗普还在仪式上指出赫格斯塞斯，称他作为国防部长的工作“非常出色”。
在民主党议员推动​​弹劾赫格塞斯的过程中，特朗普多次为赫格塞斯辩护。周二，国会山弹劾国防部长的努力失败，指控他未经国会授权对伊朗发动战争。

title_en: What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
title_zh: 乌克兰在阿布扎比与俄罗斯和美国的会谈取得了什么成果？
summary: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?
summary_zh: 乌克兰、美国和俄罗斯九个月来的首次三边会谈以交换囚犯的协议结束。这是否标志着一个ge
body_en: The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine , the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.
The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.

"We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner announced after the talks. US envoys Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Thursday, where they are due to meet President Vladimir Putin .

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had earlier suggested an exchange of "1,000 for 1,000" prisoners, or "1,500 for 1,500." Russia said a large-scale prisoner exchange with Ukraine could take place within the next two to three weeks.

Following the meetings, Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram that the parties had discussed security guarantees and that "the first step should be ending this war and ensuring Ukraine's security." He also stressed that Europe should be involved "at every stage of genuine diplomacy."
Experts interviewed by DW agree that the main outcome of the talks is humanitarian.
"The agreement on a prisoner exchange is already a major step forward," says Artjom Bronzhukov of the Ukrainian think tank Polityka.

Pavlo Lakiychuk of the Ukrainian Center for Global Studies Strategy XXI also viewed it as a "very tangible result." He told DW that "getting our people back is already a major success. That is why it is worth continuing."
A real breakthrough, he added, would be the release of civilian detainees from territories occupied since 2014, particularly people from Crimea , who have been held in Russian prisons for years.

Davyd Arakhamia, head of the ruling Servant of the People parliamentary faction and Ukraine's representative at the talks in Abu Dhabi, gave a positive assessment of the trilateral talks with the US and Russia, expressing hope that an agreement could be reached by the end of the year.

"I think the Russians came with extremely strict instructions, and it was difficult to ease the tone of the discussion. But the way the US representatives structured the talks with a view to the postwar situation in both countries opened up a dialogue, in my opinion, and allowed us to work together more productively," Arakhamia said at a joint press conference with US and Ukrainian representatives following the talks.
Iuliia Osmolovska of the Kyiv office of the international think tank GLOBSEC cautions against reading too much into the positive assessments of the talks from Washington and Kyiv.

"Diplomats taking part in negotiations will never say that everything went badly and that they have no expectations. Even when no results are achieved, they will still emphasize that the talks were constructive," she said. "For anyone familiar with diplomatic language, these are simply standard phrases."
Experts: chances for Russia-Ukraine ceasefire low as things currently stand

Osmolovska points to a joint assessment by 71 Ukrainian security and defense experts published by GLOBSEC in the summer. According to the assessment, the chances of a peace agreement or at least a ceasefire being reached this year or next stand at just 19%.

She blames this on the fact that neither side is "ready" for genuine negotiations. Russia, in particular, has yet to accept that its objectives cannot be achieved by military means. "What we are seeing now is more of a farce, an attempt by all sides to put a brave face on things and create the impression that something is moving forward," Osmolovska said.
Artjom Bronzhukov sees the talks as a way for Moscow to buy time.

"The visits by the Russian delegation, particularly under the leadership of Vladimir Medinsky, are nothing more than an attempt to stall and sell empty promises to the US administration in the form of grand agreements, in order to continue receiving so-called gestures of goodwill from Washington, such as the lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel ," the political scientist says.
body_zh: 乌克兰、美国和俄罗斯代表团于11月10日至11日在阿布扎比举行了为期两天的会谈，但没有达成停火协议。
主要成果是就囚犯交换达成了协议。
贾里德·库什纳在会谈后宣布：“我们已就最大规模的人道主义释放囚犯达成一致，明天我们将敲定具体数字。”美国特使库什纳和史蒂夫·威特科夫周四抵达莫斯科，他们将在那里会见总统弗拉基米尔·普京。
乌克兰总统泽连斯基早些时候曾建议以“1,000 人换 1,000 名”囚犯，或“1,500 人换 1,500 人”。俄罗斯表示，未来两到三周内可能会与乌克兰进行大规模的囚犯交换。
会面结束后，泽伦斯基在 Telegram 上写道，双方讨论了安全保障，“第一步应该是结束这场战争并确保乌克兰的安全”。他还强调，欧洲应该参与“真正外交的每个阶段”。
德国之声采访的专家一致认为，此次会谈的主要成果是人道主义方面的。
乌克兰智库Polityka的Artjom Bronzhukov表示：“交换囚犯的协议已经是向前迈出的重要一步。”
乌克兰第二十一届全球研究战略中心的帕夫洛·拉基丘克（Pavlo Lakiychuk）也认为这是一个“非常切实的结果”。他告诉德国之声，“让我们的员工回来已经是一个重大成功。这就是为什么值得继续下去。”
他补充说，真正的突破将是释放自 2014 年以来被占领领土上被拘留的平民，特别是来自克里米亚的人，他们已被关押在俄罗斯监狱多年。

阿拉卡米亚在会谈后与美国和乌克兰代表举行的联合新闻发布会上表示：“我认为俄罗斯人带着极其严格的指示而来，很难缓和讨论的基调。但我认为，美国代表着眼于两国战后局势而安排会谈的方式开启了对话，并使我们能够更富有成效地合作。”
国际智库 GLOBSEC 基辅办事处的尤利娅·奥斯莫洛夫斯卡 (Iuliia Osmolovska) 警告不要过度解读华盛顿和基辅对会谈的积极评价。
“参加谈判的外交官永远不会说一切都不顺利，没有任何期望。即使没有取得任何成果，他们仍然会强调谈判是建设性的，”她说。 “对于任何熟悉外交语言的人来说，这些只是标准短语。”
专家：从目前情况来看，俄罗斯和乌克兰停火的可能性很低
奥斯莫洛夫斯卡指出，GLOBSEC 今年夏天发布了 71 名乌克兰安全和国防专家的联合评估报告。据评估，今年或明年达成和平协议或至少达成停火的可能性仅为19%。
她将此归咎于双方都没有“准备好”进行真正的谈判。尤其是俄罗斯，尚未承认其目标无法通过军事手段实现。奥斯莫洛夫斯卡说：“我们现在看到的更像是一场闹剧，各方都试图勇敢地面对事情，给人留下事情正在向前发展的印象。”
阿乔姆·布龙朱科夫认为会谈是莫斯科争取时间的一种方式。
这位政治学家表示：“俄罗斯代表团的访问，特别是在弗拉基米尔·梅丁斯基领导下的访问，无非是试图拖延并向美国政府兜售大协议形式的空头承诺，以继续收到华盛顿所谓的善意姿态，例如取消对俄罗斯柴油机的制裁。”

title_en: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says
title_zh: 慈善机构称，病毒传播期间，数百万埃博拉资金失踪，员工没有拿到工资
summary: Medical staff are going unpaid, lack proper training and are struggling with shortages of essential supplies, MSF warns
summary_zh: 无国界医生警告说，医务人员没有工资，缺乏适当的培训，并且面临基本物资短缺的困境
body_en: Hundreds of millions of dollars meant to help tackle Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo are not reaching the intended recipients, a medical charity has warned.

A report from Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said that while the outbreak remained "out of control", front-line workers were going unpaid, lacked proper training and were struggling with shortages of essential supplies.
It added that in some cases ambulances had run out of fuel.
More than 5,400 people have died and 11,000 infected with Ebola in DR Congo since the outbreak was declared in May.
This makes it the second-most deadly outbreak of the disease ever recorded.
MSF has urged the Congolese government and UN agencies to "strengthen oversight and accountability" to ensure money already disbursed is effectively utilised.
This means "ensuring response personnel are properly trained, paid, equipped, and supported, and directing resources towards areas where needs are greatest", it said.
The BBC has asked the Congolese government for comment.

MSF's warning adds to concerns raised by Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) last month, when it said that $700m (£527m) out of $962m disbursed to organisations implementing Ebola response was unaccounted for.
At the time, Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya said it was too early to describe it as embezzlement, characterising the issue as a major transparency and financial reporting failure.
The Congolese health minister echoed these concerns, saying that aid agencies were required to provide details of their work so the ministry could provide oversight but that only 22% had done so.
"Our requirement is clear: transparency must be total. The response relies on a single plan, a single budget, and a single coordination," Health Minister Samuel-Roger Kamba said on X. , external
What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

In its report , external , the charity said: "Despite the vast amounts of money provided for the response, many frontline responders are left trying to contain the outbreak with empty hands and empty pockets."
It also mentioned Ebola monitoring "surveillance teams that exist on paper but are nowhere to be seen on the ground".
"Our teams are often left speechless by the dysfunctions they witness in many areas. Six months into the response, this situation is simply unacceptable," said MSF president Javid Abdelmoneim.
One important way of stopping Ebola from spreading is contact tracing - finding all those people who had come into contact with an infected person and putting them into isolation.

"Despite the resources officially allocated to this critical activity, surveillance remains deeply problematic," MSF said, adding that two-thirds of deaths were occurring in communities not treatment centres.
According to British epidemiologist Neil Ferguson, more than half of the cases are going undetected, meaning the outbreak is likely to last another year, reports the Reuters news agency.
MSF also raised concerns over "excessive concentration" of efforts in certain areas at the expense of other areas where needs were more urgent.
body_zh: 一家医疗慈善机构警告称，用于帮助刚果民主共和国应对埃博拉病毒的数亿美元并未到达预期受益人手中。
无国界医生组织（MSF）的一份报告称，虽然疫情仍然“失控”，但一线工人却拿不到工资，缺乏适当的培训，并且面临必需品短缺的困境。
它还补充说，在某些情况下，救护车的燃油已经耗尽。
自 5 月份宣布埃博拉疫情爆发以来，刚果民主共和国已有 5,400 多人死亡，11,000 人感染埃博拉病毒。
这使其成为有记录以来第二致命的疾病爆发。
无国界医生敦促刚果政府和联合国机构“加强监督和问责”，以确保已发放的资金得到有效利用。
报告称，这意味着“确保响应人员得到适当的培训、报酬、装备和支持，并将资源投入最需要的领域”。
BBC 已要求刚果政府发表评论。
无国界医生组织的警告加剧了非洲疾病控制和预防中心 (Africa CDC) 上个月提出的担忧，当时该中心表示，在支付给实施埃博拉应对措施的组织的 9.62 亿美元中，有 7 亿美元（5.27 亿英镑）下落不明。
当时，非洲疾病预防控制中心负责人让·卡塞亚表示，现在将其描述为贪污还为时过早，并将该问题定性为重大的透明度和财务报告失败。
刚果卫生部长回应了这些担忧，称援助机构必须提供其工作细节，以便卫生部能够提供监督，但只有 22% 的机构这样做了。
“我们的要求很明确：必须完全透明。应对措施依赖于单一计划、单一预算和单一协调，”卫生部长塞缪尔-罗杰·卡姆巴 (Samuel-Roger Kamba) 在 X. 上表示。
什么是埃博拉病毒？为什么阻止最新的疫情如此困难？
该慈善机构在其对外报告中表示：“尽管为应对工作提供了大量资金，但许多前线救援人员仍然两手空空、口袋空空，试图控制疫情。”
它还提到埃博拉监测“纸面上存在但在实地却无处可见的监测小组”。
无国界医生组织主席贾维德·阿卜杜勒莫奈姆 (Javid Abdelmoneim) 表示：“我们的团队常常因在许多领域目睹的功能失调而无言以对。在做出反应六个月后，这种情况简直令人无法接受。”
阻止埃博拉病毒传播的一个重要方法是接触者追踪——找到所有与感染者接触过的人并将他们隔离。
无国界医生表示：“尽管官方为这项关键活动分配了资源，但监测仍然存在严重问题。”他补充说，三分之二的死亡发生在社区而不是治疗中心。
据路透社报道，英国流行病学家尼尔·弗格森表示，超过一半的病例未被发现，这意味着疫情可能会再持续一年。
无国界医生还对“过度集中”某些领域的工作而忽视其他需求更为紧迫的领域表示担忧。

title_en: Eight killed in Colombian air strike targeting Gulf Clan gang
title_zh: 哥伦比亚针对海湾部落帮派的空袭造成八人死亡
summary: A suspected gang leader considered a "priority target" was among those killed, the Colombian president says.
summary_zh: 哥伦比亚总统表示，被杀者中有一名被视为“优先目标”的犯罪团伙头目嫌疑人。
body_en: Colombia: Eight killed in air strike targeting Gulf Clan gang - BBC News

A senior leader of Colombia's largest criminal gang, the Gulf Clan, is among eight people killed in an air strike carried out by the country's armed forces, according to President Abelardo de la Espriella.
De la Espriella said he had personally authorised the bombing targeting the Gulf Clan in the province of Antioquia, in north-west Colombia.
He added that Haminton Mosquera, whom he described as a senior member of the crime gang and one of 10 "priority targets" for Colombia's security forces, had been "brought down".
De la Espriella was elected in June after campaigning on a promise to crack down on Colombia's powerful criminal gangs, including by launching air strikes.

In a post on X , external , he said that Mosquera was suspected of having ordered attacks against the security forces, including the murder of a police officer in the municipality of Tarazá last year.
The Gulf Clan has been engaging in criminal activities for decades, mainly trafficking cocaine from Colombia to destinations in the US and Europe but also illegal mining and people smuggling.
The US added it to its list of Foreign Terrorist Organisations (FTOs) last year.
In his post, President de la Espriella said that "the offensive won't stop" and vowed to regain control of areas currently controlled by criminal organisations such as the Gulf Clan.

While his offensive against criminal gangs has been welcomed by many living in areas where extortion and gang violence are rampant, de la Espriella has faced criticism for the way he has made some of his announcements on security.
Less than a month after taking office, he published a video showing him walking among 23 body bags containing the remains of 23 people killed in an air strike on a suspected guerrilla camp.
On Wednesday, he shared a photo , external in which he can be seen writing his campaign slogan, "Welcome to the miracle homeland" on a bomb.
He has also defended his decision to wear an army uniform at a recent event in Cúcuta at which he confronted a detainee suspected of being a Farc rebel.
"What did you make of the bomb I sent you, signed by me?," the president can be heard asking the man.

He later told journalists that he wore the uniform because "I am a soldier of the homeland. That's why I dress like a soldier, because I came to serve Colombia. Because I honour the heroes, police officers and military."
Additional reporting by BBC Monitoring's Luis Fajardo.

body_zh: 哥伦比亚：针对海湾部族帮派的空袭造成八人死亡 -_澳门赌博平台
哥伦比亚总统阿韦拉多·德拉埃斯普里埃拉称，哥伦比亚最大犯罪团伙海湾帮的一名高级头目在该国武装部队发动的空袭中丧生，其中有八人死亡。
德拉埃斯普里埃拉表示，他亲自授权对哥伦比亚西北部安蒂奥基亚省的海湾部落进行轰炸。
他补充说，哈明顿·莫斯克拉（Haminton Mosquera）已被“打倒”，他将其描述为犯罪团伙的高级成员，也是哥伦比亚安全部队的 10 个“优先目标”之一。
德拉埃斯普里埃拉在竞选时承诺打击哥伦比亚强大的犯罪团伙，包括发动空袭，并于六月当选。
他在《X》、《外部》上发帖称，莫斯克拉涉嫌下令袭击安全部队，包括去年在塔拉萨市谋杀一名警察。
海湾集团几十年来一直从事犯罪活动，主要从哥伦比亚贩运可卡因到美国和欧洲的目的地，但也进行非法采矿和人口走私。
美国去年将其列入外国恐怖组织（FTO）名单。
德拉埃斯普里埃拉总统在帖子中表示，“攻势不会停止”，并发誓要重新控制目前由海湾部族等犯罪组织控制的地区。
尽管德拉埃斯普里埃拉对犯罪团伙的进攻受到了居住在敲诈勒索和帮派暴力猖獗地区的许多人的欢迎，但德拉埃斯普里埃拉因其发布一些安全公告的方式而面临批评。
上任不到一个月，他发布了一段视频，显示他在23个尸袋中行走，里面装着23名在空袭疑似游击队营地中丧生的人的遗体。
周三，他分享了一张外部照片，可以看到他在一枚炸弹上写下了自己的竞选口号“欢迎来到奇迹家园”。
他还为自己在最近在库库塔举行的一次活动中穿军装的决定进行了辩护，当时他与一名疑似哥伦比亚革命武装力量叛乱分子的被拘留者对峙。
“你对我寄给你的、有我签名的炸弹做了什么？”可以听到总统问该男子。
他后来告诉记者，他穿这身制服是因为“我是祖国的一名士兵。这就是为什么我穿得像一名士兵，因为我是来为哥伦比亚服务的。因为我向英雄、警察和军队致敬。”
BBC 监测部门的路易斯·法哈多 (Luis Fajardo) 进行了补充报道。

title_en: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story
title_zh: 津巴布韦作家 Simbarashe Kundizeza 不得使用人工智能撰写获奖故事
summary: After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’ The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, afte
summary_zh: 经过一个月的调查，得出的结论是，昆迪泽扎获得 10,000 英镑凯恩奖的小说《蓝色斗士》是“人写的”。
body_en: After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’

The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation.
Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter , which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October.

Five days later, the Atlantic published an article titled “Yet another literary prize winner seems to be AI”, in which the author and journalist Vauhini Vara said the AI-detection software Pangram, which itself uses AI, had deemed the story to be almost completely artificially generated.

The Caine prize chair, Ellah Wakatama, said in a statement : “From our detailed investigation, we feel the evidence is clear: The Blue Fighter was human-written. We now look forward to awarding and celebrating Simbarashe Steyn Kundizeza … before the end of the year.”
She said: “When concerns were raised, we have a duty as an organisation to look at them carefully and fairly,” adding that the prize had taken a “human-centred” approach to its investigation.

“Our review included interviews with the author, the 2026 judging panel and The Shallow Tales Review, where the story was first published,” Wakatama said. “It also included independent and expert-led metadata analysis of drafts written by the author.”

Kundizeza, who had strongly denied using generative AI to write the story, said he was “relieved” that the allegations had been dismissed after the investigation. “It was not necessary in the first place, I am happy to put all this behind me and continue with my writing journey,” he said.
Vara’s article prompted outrage online, with many claiming that Black writers, and Africans in particular, were being unfairly singled out by allegations of the use of AI.
body_zh: 经过一个月的调查，得出的结论是，昆迪泽扎获得 10,000 英镑凯恩奖的小说《蓝色斗士》是“人写的”
久负盛名的非洲作家凯恩奖经过一个月的调查后得出结论，津巴布韦作家辛巴拉什·昆迪泽萨 (Simbarashe Kundizeza) 的作品是“人类撰写的”，因此被取消使用人工智能撰写获奖短篇小说的资格。
昆迪泽扎的小说《蓝色斗士》讲述了一个家庭在父亲投资鱼缸后财富不断下降的故事，该小说于 10 月 6 日被宣布为 10,000 英镑奖金的获奖者。
五天后，《大西洋月刊》发表了一篇题为《又一个文学奖得主似乎是人工智能》的文章，作者兼记者沃希尼·瓦拉 (Vauhini Vara) 表示，本身使用人工智能的人工智能检测软件 Pangram 认为这个故事几乎完全是人工生成的。
凯恩奖主席埃拉·瓦卡塔玛 (Ellah Wakatama) 在一份声明中表示：“根据我们的详细调查，我们认为证据很明确：《蓝色战士》是人类编写的。我们现在期待在年底之前授予并庆祝 Simbarashe Steyn Kundizeza。”
她说：“当人们提出担忧时，我们作为一个组织有责任仔细、公平地看待它们，”并补充说，该奖项采取了“以人为本”的调查方法。
“我们的评论包括对作者、2026 年评审团以及故事首次发表的《浅薄故事评论》的采访，”若玉说。 “它还包括对作者撰写的草稿进行独立且由专家主导的元数据分析。”
昆迪泽扎强烈否认使用生成式人工智能来撰写这篇报道，他表示，调查后指控被驳回，他感到“松了一口气”。 “一开始就没有必要，我很高兴把这一切抛在脑后，继续我的写作之旅，”他说。
瓦拉的文章在网上引起了愤怒，许多人声称黑人作家，尤其是非洲人，因使用人工智能的指控而受到不公平的对待。

title_en: Democrat Scott Colom makes history as Mississippi's first black senator since 19th Century
title_zh: 民主党人斯科特·科洛姆 (Scott Colom) 赢得密西西比州参议院竞选，该党意外获胜
summary: In a state Trump won two years ago by 22 points, Colom's victory extends a string of Democratic wins in the Senate.
summary_zh: 科罗姆的胜利使他成为 140 多年来第一位当选美国参议员的密西西比州黑人。
body_en: By Brandon Drenon , Jackson, Mississippi and Sareen Habeshian
Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades.
Colom's victory makes him the first black person from Mississippi to be seated in the US Senate since Blanche Bruce served from 1875 to 1881.
Fewer than five thousand votes out of nearly a million counted separated him from his Republican opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith.
The result means the Democrats will hold 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with a knife-edge race in Alaska still to be called.
Before Scott Colom, these two men were the last black US senators in Mississippi
Colom, 43, won with 49.2% of the vote. Hyde-Smith, who received 48.7%, congratulated Colom in a video posted on X on Wednesday evening and wished him well.
"While this was not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said.
The contest was not considered to be in play until the final weeks of the campaign, given President Donald Trump won the state in the 2024 election by more than 22 points.
Colom offered a victory speech on the campus of Tougaloo College, met by hundreds of cheering supporters standing side-by-side under the night sky.
Excitement filled the air as he thanked them for the support over the days of waiting for a result since the 4 November election.
"They did not believe a moment like this was possible, but I kept the faith," Colom said.
"It's not something that I did y'all," he continued. "It's something we did."
"In Mississippi, it's local people that make the difference."
Dozens of people were gathered at the Mississippi HQ of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in Jackson on Wednesday when Colom's victory was announced.
The room burst into deafening applause and cheers.
"This is an amazing result," said Leon Russell, chairman of the NAACP board.
"This is purely the work of particularly the black community," he continued. "There was not a whole lot of money, but there was a whole lot of organising.
Across the room, filled with people embracing, Amber Thomas sat, revelling in the victory.
body_zh: 作者：布兰登·德雷农 (Brandon Drenon)，密西西比州杰克逊和萨琳·哈贝希安 (Sareen Habeshian)
民主党人斯科特·科洛姆 (Scott Colom) 在密西西比州的美国参议院竞选中获胜，为该党在这个几十年来一直选举共和党人的极度保守的州取得了令人震惊的胜利。
科罗姆的胜利使他成为自 1875 年至 1881 年布兰奇·布鲁斯 (Blanche Bruce) 任职以来第一位在美国参议院任职的密西西比州黑人。
在统计的近百万张选票中，只有不到五千张选票将他与共和党对手、现任议员辛迪·海德·史密斯分开。
结果意味着民主党将在 100 名议员的参议院中占据 55 个席位，阿拉斯加的一场激烈角逐仍悬而未决。
在斯科特·科洛姆之前，这两个人是密西西比州最后一位黑人美国参议员
43 岁的科罗姆以 49.2% 的选票获胜。海德-史密斯获得了 48.7% 的支持率，他在周三晚上发布在 X 上的一段视频中向科洛姆表示祝贺，并祝愿他一切顺利。
“虽然这不是我们努力或希望的结果，但我尊重密西西比州选民的决定，”她说。
鉴于唐纳德·特朗普总统在 2024 年大选中以超过 22 个百分点的优势赢得了该州，这场竞争直到竞选活动的最后几周才被认为开始进行。
科罗姆在图加卢学院校园发表了胜利演讲，数百名欢呼的支持者在夜空下并肩站立。
当他感谢他们自 11 月 4 日选举以来等待结果的日子里给予的支持时，空气中充满了兴奋。
“他们不相信这样的时刻是可能的，但我保持了信念，”科罗姆说。
“你们大家这不是我做的，”他继续说道。 “这是我们所做的事情。”
“在密西西比州，改变现状的是当地人。”
周三，当科罗姆获胜的消息宣布时，数十人聚集在位于杰克逊的全国有色人种协进会（NAACP）密西西比州总部。
房间里爆发出震耳欲聋的掌声和欢呼声。
“这是一个令人惊奇的结果，”全国有色人种协进会董事会主席莱昂·拉塞尔说。
“这纯粹是黑人社区的工作，”他继续说道。 “虽然没有很多钱，但有很多组织工作。
房间的另一边，挤满了拥抱的人们，安布尔·托马斯坐着，陶醉在胜利之中。

title_en: Five new miniature frog species found in eastern Himalayas
title_zh: 喜马拉雅山脉东部发现了五种新的微型青蛙物种
summary: Scientists say the frogs evolved as the Himalayas rose and the Asian monsoon took shape.
summary_zh: 科学家表示，青蛙是随着喜马拉雅山的上升和亚洲季风的形成而进化的。
body_en: Rare frog species reveal overlooked Himalayan diversity of Arunachal Pradesh - BBC News
Scientists have discovered five new species of tiny horned frogs in India's eastern Himalayas, more than doubling the number of known species in the group.
A team of scientists from University of Delhi and Harvard University made the discoveries after five years of fieldwork, identifying the frogs as members of the Jingophrys group.
Among them is Jingophrys tanogogo - or the snail-eating horned frog - the first frog known in India to feed on snails and the first member of its family recorded with such a diet.
The research suggest the Himalayas have played a much larger role in frog evolution than previously thought and highlight the region as an overlooked hotspot for biodiversity.
The Himalayas, stretching from tropical forests to alpine meadows, are among the world's richest biodiversity regions.
Despite drawing interest from scientists and researchers, many parts here have not been fully explored.
The state of Arunachal Pradesh particularly has emerged as one of its least-studied regions.
Dr Sonali Garg, who led the study at Harvard University's Museum of Comparative Zoology, said the research highlights how significant evolutionary changes can go unnoticed in little-studied species.

The study - called two-fold hidden diversity of diminutive horned frogs (Megophryinae: Jingophrys) - was conducted by Garg along with her colleague James Hanken and Delhi University's SD Biju, Tage Tajo and Radhakrishna Upadhyaya K.
It was published on 11 November in the Royal Society Open Science journal.
"Some of the new species are extremely secretive and found in remote forests only during a short breeding season," says Biju.
Researchers say further studies will have to done to better understand their biology and conservation needs.

DNA analysis showed the horned frogs rapidly diversified into multiple species in the eastern Himalayas as the mountain range rose and the Asian monsoon took shape over millions of years, helping drive the evolution of the region's plants and wildlife.

The researchers said in a statement that local tribes gave them essential field support and knowledge that helped make the discoveries possible. Some of the species were named after these communities.
The Tanii horned frog (Jingophrys taniitatii), for instance, is named by combining the name of the Tanii tribe in the region with the word 'tatti' - frog in the local Apatani language.

The new species have been named Jingophrys taniitatii (Tanii horned frog), Jingophrys tanogogo (snail-eating horned frog), Jingophrys siangensis (Siang horned frog), Jingophrys hrdy (Hrdy's horned frog) and Jingophrys wularsoni (Wu-Larson's horned frog).
body_zh: 稀有青蛙物种揭示了阿鲁纳恰尔邦被忽视的喜马拉雅多样性 - BBC 新闻
科学家在印度喜马拉雅山脉东部发现了五种新的小角蛙物种，是该类群已知物种数量的两倍多。
来自德里大学和哈佛大学的科学家团队经过五年的实地考察后取得了这一发现，确定这些青蛙是金戈弗里斯群的成员。
其中包括金格弗里斯·塔诺戈戈（Jingophrys tanogogo），即食蜗牛角蛙，它是印度已知的第一只以蜗牛为食的青蛙，也是记录在案的第一个以蜗牛为食的青蛙家族成员。
研究表明，喜马拉雅山脉在青蛙进化中发挥的作用比之前想象的要大得多，并强调该地区是一个被忽视的生物多样性热点地区。
喜马拉雅山脉从热带森林一直延伸到高山草甸，是世界上生物多样性最丰富的地区之一。
尽管引起了科学家和研究人员的兴趣，但这里的许多部分尚未得到充分探索。
阿鲁纳恰尔邦尤其成为研究最少的地区之一。
哈佛大学比较动物学博物馆这项研究的领导者索纳利·加格博士表示，这项研究强调了在很少被研究的物种中，重大的进化变化可能会被忽视。
这项研究被称为小角蛙（Megophryinae：Jingophrys）的双重隐藏多样性，由 Garg 与她的同事 James Hanken 以及德里大学的 SD Biju、Tage Tajo 和 Radhakrishna Upadhyaya K 共同进行。
它于 11 月 11 日发表在《皇家学会开放科学》杂志上。
比朱说：“一些新物种极其隐秘，只有在短暂的繁殖季节才能在偏远的森林中发现。”
研究人员表示，必须进行进一步的研究才能更好地了解它们的生物学和保护需求。
DNA分析显示，数百万年来，随着山脉的上升和亚洲季风的形成，喜马拉雅山脉东部的角蛙迅速多样化为多种物种，推动了该地区植物和野生动物的进化。
研究人员在一份声明中表示，当地部落为他们提供了必要的现场支持和知识，帮助他们实现了这一发现。有些物种是以这些群落命名的。
例如，塔尼角蛙 (Jingophrys taniitatii) 的命名是将该地区塔尼部落的名称与当地阿帕塔尼语中的“tatti”（青蛙）一词结合起来。
新物种被命名为Jingophrys taniitatii（塔尼角蛙）、Jingophrys tanogogo（吃蜗牛角蛙）、Jingophrys siangensis（西安角蛙）、Jingophrys hrdy（赫迪角蛙）和Jingophrys wularsoni（吴-拉森角蛙）。

title_en: Russian court jails rights lawyer for 12 years on treason charge
title_zh: 俄罗斯法院以叛国罪判处维权律师12年监禁

body_en: Russian court jails rights lawyer for 12 years on treason charge | Courts News | Al Jazeera
Share Russian court jails rights lawyer for 12 years on treason charge on social media

A court in Russia’s Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad has sentenced a 66-year-old rights lawyer to 12 years in prison for treason, after prosecutors accused her of passing sensitive information to Ukraine.

The court imposed the sentence on Thursday on Maria Bontsler, according to the rights group Slovo Zashchite, which said she had worked with a number of defendants accused of political offences in Kaliningrad.

A court statement posted on Telegram did not name her, but said she had been detained by the FSB intelligence agency on allegations of passing information to Ukraine beginning in 2024 about security officers in Kaliningrad.
Prosecutors also alleged she gave Ukraine information on criminal cases in the exclave that were of interest to Kyiv, the statement said.
She was also given an extra year of restrictions on her activity. Prosecutors had sought 15 years, according to Slovo Zashchite.

Slovo Zashchite said the trial was held behind closed doors, with Bontsler and her lawyers prevented from attending, and that she was allowed only to make a closing statement. It said her lawyers argued that none of the information cited by prosecutors was secret, and that she had been in ill health in detention.

Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, parliament has approved laws that make public actions aimed at “discrediting” the army illegal and ban the spread of “fake news” about the armed forces.

Russian courts have also jailed lawyers who took on politically sensitive cases. In January 2025, a court sentenced three lawyers of the late opposition leader Alexey Navalny to between three and a half and five and a half years on “extremism” charges, in a case widely seen as an effort to discourage defence lawyers from taking political cases.

title_en: Former Ukrainian foreign minister discusses how to bridge gaps between Ukraine, Russia
title_zh: 乌克兰前外长讨论如何弥合乌克兰与俄罗斯之间的分歧
summary: NPR's A Martinez asks Ukraine's former Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba for his proposals to close gaps in talks between Russia, Ukraine and Europe.
summary_zh: 美国国家公共广播电台的马丁内斯向乌克兰前外长德米特罗·库莱巴询问有关缩小俄罗斯、乌克兰和欧洲之间谈判分歧的建议。
body_en: Former Ukrainian foreign minister discusses how to bridge gaps between Ukraine, Russia NPR's A Martinez asks Ukraine's former Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba for his proposals to close gaps in talks between Russia, Ukraine and Europe.
NPR's A Martinez asks Ukraine's former Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba for his proposals to close gaps in talks between Russia, Ukraine and Europe.

Let's hear from a former Ukrainian official with extensive experience negotiating on behalf of the country. Dmytro Kuleba was foreign minister for Ukraine from 2020 to 2024. Today, he's a senior fellow at the Harvard Kennedy School's Belfer Center. Minister, Russia and Ukraine agreed, at least in principle, to a large-scale prisoner exchange as part of these talks. They've done that before. Were you hoping for more progress to be made with these talks?

DMYTRO KULEBA: No, I didn't. And I actually have to say that prisoner swaps should be taking place outside of the scope of political negotiations as a part of regular humanitarian effort. But I don't see any driver behind Russia's position that has changed recently in the trajectory of genuine negotiations in good faith.
MARTÍNEZ: So as far as making progress toward ending the war, these prisoner exchanges to you means nothing?

KULEBA: Well, prisoners exchange means the world to every Ukrainian because our people are coming back home to their family from Russian prisons, where they're subjected to torture and disregarding treatment. So it's a big deal. But it has zero impact on the progress on the political track towards ending the conflict.

MARTÍNEZ: When it comes to Europe's role in these talks, we know that Vladimir Putin does not want Europe involved. And the U.S. has said that NATO allies are essential to a lasting peace. Is there a way for U.S. envoys to persuade Russia, to persuade Vladimir Putin to accept European involvement in these talks?

KULEBA: Having Europeans at the table costs nothing to Russia, but it will try to sell their presence at the highest price possible. This is their negotiating strategy. It just doesn't make sense to negotiate without Europe because the solution, the possible outcome of these negotiations will only hold if Ukraine and the rest of Europe agree to it and sign up. If Europe doesn't sign up, no agreement will be possible because this war is happening in Europe. It's essentially a European war with global impact.
MARTÍNEZ: If European presence in these talks doesn't cost Russia anything, why doesn't the U.S. basically just hold Vladimir Putin's hands to the fire on this and insist on them being there?
KULEBA: Could you give me one example from the last two years when the United States held President Putin's arms to the fire?
KULEBA: That's not the way this administration treats President Putin. They actually more kind of care for his hands than want to cause harm to them.

MARTÍNEZ: So if you know that, minister - and obviously, Vladimir Putin probably knows that - then what are the chances that any progress can be made? All he has to do is just continue to hold the line.

KULEBA: Well, that's exactly what he has been doing for the last two years. And this is what I believe, regrettably, he will continue to do in the coming years. He just needs to continue engaging with his - engage the United States, court President Trump in a way that will give him enough of a reason to believe that an agreement is possible, and that Putin is seeking an agreement but just needs to be accommodated on one or two more points.
MARTÍNEZ: Do you think that Democratic control of the new Congress, the upcoming Congress, will somehow alter the course of these talks or maybe the future of U.S. support for Ukraine?

KULEBA: Well, foreign policy, especially in negotiations with foreign leaders, stays firmly in the hands of the president of the United States of America. So, yes, of course I expect a reinvigorated role of Congress on the Ukrainian file. But I believe President Trump will continue his policies.
MARTÍNEZ: Dmytro Kuleba served as Ukraine's foreign minister from 2020 to 2024. He's now at the Harvard Kennedy School's Belfer Center. Minister, thank you very much for your time.

body_zh: 乌克兰前外长讨论如何弥合乌克兰、俄罗斯之间的分歧 NPR 的马丁内斯向乌克兰前外长德米特罗·库莱巴询问有关缩小俄罗斯、乌克兰和欧洲之间谈判分歧的建议。
美国国家公共广播电台的马丁内斯向乌克兰前外长德米特罗·库莱巴询问有关缩小俄罗斯、乌克兰和欧洲之间谈判分歧的建议。
让我们听听一位拥有丰富代表国家谈判经验的前乌克兰官员的看法。德米特罗·库莱巴 (Dmytro Kuleba) 在 2020 年至 2024 年期间担任乌克兰外交部长。如今，他是哈佛大学肯尼迪学院贝尔弗中心的高级研究员。作为会谈的一部分，俄罗斯和乌克兰至少在原则上同意大规模交换囚犯。他们以前就这么做过。您是否希望这些会谈取得更多进展？
DMYTRO KULEBA： 不，我没有。事实上我不得不说，囚犯交换应该在政治谈判范围之外进行，作为常规人道主义努力的一部分。但我认为俄罗斯立场背后的任何推动因素最近在真诚谈判的轨道上没有发生改变。
马丁内斯：那么就结束战争的进展而言，这些囚犯交换对你来说毫无意义？
库列巴：嗯，囚犯交换对每个乌克兰人来说意义重大，因为我们的人民正在从俄罗斯监狱回到家人身边，他们在那里遭受酷刑和无视待遇。所以这是一件大事。但这对结束冲突的政治进程的影响为零。
马丁内斯：当谈到欧洲在这些谈判中的作用时，我们知道弗拉基米尔·普京不希望欧洲参与其中。美国表示，北约盟国对于持久和平至关重要。美国特使有办法说服俄罗斯、说服弗拉基米尔·普京接受欧洲参与这些谈判吗？
库莱巴：让欧洲人参与进来对俄罗斯来说没有任何成本，但俄罗斯会尽力以尽可能高的价格出售欧洲人的存在。这是他们的谈判策略。在没有欧洲的情况下进行谈判是没有意义的，因为只有乌克兰和欧洲其他国家同意并签署，解决方案和这些谈判的可能结果才会成立。如果欧洲不签署，就不可能达成协议，因为这场战争正在欧洲发生。这本质上是一场具有全球影响的欧洲战争。
马丁内斯：如果欧洲参加这些谈判不会让俄罗斯付出任何代价，那么美国为什么不直接阻止普京并坚持让他们参加呢？
库莱巴：你能给我举一个过去两年美国将普京总统的手臂付之一炬的例子吗？
库莱巴：这不是本届政府对待普京总统的方式。他们实际上更关心他的手，而不是想要伤害他的手。
马丁内斯：部长，如果您知道这一点——显然弗拉基米尔·普京可能也知道这一点——那么取得进展的可能性有多大？他所要做的就是继续坚守阵地。
库莱巴：嗯，这正是他过去两年一直在做的事情。遗憾的是，我相信这就是他在未来几年将继续做的事情。他只需要继续与美国接触，向特朗普总统示好，让他有足够的理由相信达成协议是可能的，而普京正在寻求达成协议，但只需要在一两点上得到满足。
马丁内斯：您认为民主党对新国会、即将召开的国会的控制会以某种方式改变这些谈判的进程，或者可能改变美国对乌克兰支持的未来吗？
库莱巴：外交政策，特别是与外国领导人的谈判，牢牢掌握在美利坚合众国总统手中。所以，是的，我当然希望国会在乌克兰档案中发挥新的作用。但我相信特朗普总统将继续他的政策。
马丁内斯：德米特罗·库莱巴 (Dmytro Kuleba) 在 2020 年至 2024 年期间担任乌克兰外交部长。他现在在哈佛大学肯尼迪学院贝尔弗中心工作。部长，非常感谢您抽出时间。

title_en: Former U.S. Ambassador William Taylor discusses the latest Russia-Ukraine talks
title_zh: 美国前大使威廉·泰勒讨论最新的俄罗斯-乌克兰会谈
summary: NPR's A Martinez speaks with former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine, William Taylor, about the ongoing peace talks between the U.S., Russia and Ukraine.
summary_zh: NPR 的 A 马丁内斯与前美国驻乌克兰大使威廉·泰勒谈论了美国、俄罗斯和乌克兰之间正在进行的和平谈判。
body_en: Former U.S. Ambassador William Taylor discusses the latest Russia-Ukraine talks NPR's A Martinez speaks with former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine, William Taylor, about the ongoing peace talks between the U.S., Russia and Ukraine.
NPR's A Martinez speaks with former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine, William Taylor, about the ongoing peace talks between the U.S., Russia and Ukraine.

William Taylor has been listening along with us. He served as U.S. ambassador to Ukraine during the George W. Bush and Obama administrations. Ambassador, so I know no major breakthroughs, but a prisoner swap. So is this an accomplishment, nonetheless?

WILLIAM TAYLOR: Not that great, A. Of course, it's good to have prisoners come back. That's always a good thing. But what they're really after is ending the war. They want a ceasefire. And they apparently made no progress toward that.
